judged_before.why: the first judge reached its 30 minutes with no verdict

items.evidence: examen leverage play <runs>/day-engine-2 --ticks 2: screen title, JSON with every key the brief names (tick..records), no-season defaults as listed.
--frame f_day.png --size 800x480 after a run wrote an 800x480 PNG (opened and viewed).

Texts, menu_index 0 and Up/Down stops are right, but Quit (enter on index 4 at tick 5) does not end the run: --ticks 20 printed tick 20 with screen title, not the state as it stood at the quit (README admits the run goes on counting ticks).

Settings run with --at each tick: Language en<->es, Difficulty easy..hard, Season 7<->3 change and stop at the ends; defaults English/Normal/7 days with the exact texts; Escape and Enter on Back go to the title.
Set es/easy/3 in one run; a second run on the same --settings folder started es easy 3; a fresh folder gave en normal 7, slots [null,null,null], stamps [], records [].

In Spanish the title, settings (switching at once: Ajustes/Idioma: Espanol) and morning texts were all Spanish; strings.json has en and es with the same 111 keys, the only identical ones being the name and words that are the same in both languages (Normal, no, letters).
modules/work/data/strings.json holds an en and an es table; README 'Adding a language' says how.
Fresh folder, Enter on New season: ['New season','Slot 1: Empty','Slot 2: Empty','Slot 3: Empty']; Escape went to title.
Enter on slot 2: morning, day 1, slot 2, coins 50, rep 50, all stocks [], prices 4/6/11/14/7/9, upgrades [], crate_limit 8, order null, texts Morning, Day 1 of 7, Coins: 50.
Easy+3 days: coins 60, 'Dia 1 de 3', forecast 3 entries; Hard: coins 40; after changing settings to easy/3 and Continue the season still showed season_difficulty hard, length 7.
Forecast 7 entries of sun/cloud/rain/heat; weather and 'Weather: Heat'/'Weather: Cloud' follow the day; seed 1 gave the same forecast in separate runs, seeds 2-4 other ones.
Wholesale seen across seeds 1-4 and days 1-3 all in base-1..base+2 (e.g. apples 2-4, cheese 5-7, fish 6-7, honey 4-6); rows read 'Apples: 2 a unit, stock 0'.
Enter on Apples at 2: coins 50->38, apples [{units 6, days_left 5}], second lot -> one batch 12, row 'stock 12'; honey batch days_left null; bread days_left 1.
With 14 coins Enter on Fish (36) changed nothing and showed 'Not enough coins' until the next word (accept). The 99-unit cap could not be reached in a run.
Day 1 order null; day 2 'Order: 6 Flowers for 63' (6*7*3/2), accept -> taken true and 'Order taken: 6 Flowers for 63', second accept changed nothing; other orders 4 Cheese for 66, 6 Cheese for 99.
A later run on the kept folder showed title New season, Continue, Records, ... and slot row 'Slot 1: Day 2 of 7, 58 coins' (format as asked); slots entry {day,coins,length,difficulty}.

Continue in a later headless run gave day 2 wholesale 3/4/5/7/4/5 and order 4 Cheese for 66, but the season was saved with 2/2/7/6/3/5 and 6 Flowers for 63 (same within one run). Cause: the saved season seed is a 64-bit number kept as a JSON float (-7135811184969857000), so precision is lost.

Escape on Morning -> Paused [Paused, Resume, Title]; on Day the clock stood at 6 over 40 ticks and Escape resumed with the same state; Title went to title and the slot stayed at 58 coins without that Morning's bread/honey lots.
New season stall: cursor (0,0), apples, texts Stall, Good: Apples, Price: 4, Stock: 12, Crates: 0 of 8.
Left/Down at (0,0) stayed; Up -> (0,1), Up again stayed; Right stopped at x 5.
prev_good from apples gave honey ('Good: Honey','Price: 9','Stock: 0'); next_good steps apples->bread->...->flowers and honey->apples, texts following.
Puts added cells with good; with 8 crates put at (5,0) changed nothing; put on occupied cell nothing; take on empty nothing; take at (4,0) -> 7 of 8, put again -> 8 of 8.
13 price_up on bread stopped at 18; 5 price_down on apples stopped at 1; Price text followed.
Stall layout and prices (bread 18, apples 2 etc.) were the same the next day and after Pause>Title>Continue in a later run.
Enter on stall: screen day, clock 0, speed slow, '08:00', 'Speed: Slow', taken/served/walked_out/passed 0, visitors list filled.
My checker on 6 days (seeds 1-4): ids 1..n, minutes strictly increasing in 0..479, types valid, distinct wants 2/1/2/3; same seed same list, other seeds other lists.
Mixed run: 100 slow ticks -> 5 min, 200 fast -> +40, 50 hold -> +0 (screen day), 1 rush -> +1, 100 rush -> +99, 30 slow after -> +1 with remainder kept; time and Speed texts followed.
finish on day 1 seed 1 gave evening clock 480 with taken 102, served 11, walked 0, passed 22, coins 88, rep 61, the same as the per-minute rush run.
Day 3 (season C) at rush vs slow/fast/hold/rush/slow/finish: both taken 186, served 32, passed 29, walked 0.
Checker over every minute of 6 days: each visitor on the aisle at x = clock - m for m..m+5 and off from m+6.
Checker: every take was from the front cell of its column, back cell only with a non-empty basket (or Sign), always a wanted good not yet in the basket; 0 violations.
Cooks took 2 apples at 4 at their column's minute with budget 8 lower; the price-5 cook and the 6/7 tourist cases were not run.
Checker: no take exceeded budget_left; units held in all baskets never exceeded stock, every minute of 6 days.
Checker: queued visitors always joined = minute + 6; passed counts matched empty-basket leavers (e.g. 22 on day 1).
Ends = start + 2 + goods, paid totals with bargain tenth off, served/taken/sales all matched; that units leave the batch with the fewest days_left first was not observed (all units sold).
Checker: no minute with a free till and a non-empty queue; visitors reached a till at m+6 when free.
No queued wait ever reached patience, but no visitor walked out in any run (queue at most 1), so the walk-out effects were not seen.
At clock 480 screen evening with aisle, queue and tills empty and walked_out/passed unchanged by the end.
Second till bought: tills has 2 entries, visitors 5 and 6 served together (minutes 75-76), new visitor went to till 1 when both free.
Sign was bought on one run but no back-row crate had stock on that day, so the effect was not seen.
Taken flowers order with 6 in stock: 'Order delivered: 63', coins up 63, units gone; with none in stock 'Order failed' and rep -5; untaken order: no line, nothing changed.
Bread bought that Morning spoiled that evening (spoiled 6, line 'spoiled 6'); honey never spoiled; fish spoiling on the next day's evening was not observed (only seen on a heat day).
Heat day: apples days_left 5->3 without Cool box, 5->4 with it; fish 2 spoiled on heat.
Rent: 28 at Normal with 4 crates, Rent: 31 at Easy with 8 crates; Hard (30) not observed.
Evening texts: Evening, Day N of M, Taken/Served/Walked out/Passed matching state, per-good 'Apples: sold 6, spoiled 0, left 0', Rent, Coins, Reputation, 'Tomorrow: Heat'.
Upgrades: ['Upgrades','Coins: 88','Next day','Second till: 80','Cool box: 40','Sign: 30','Extra crates: 50','Awning: 35']; Next day -> Morning day 2.
Sign 88->58, 'Sign: owned', again no change; Second till with 58 -> 'Not enough coins'; Extra crates -> crate_limit 12, 'Crates: 8 of 12'.
Coins -26 after rent: 'Bankrupt' on evening, slots all null, Enter -> ['Bankrupt','Score: 0','Days: 2','Best: 0','Enter: title'], record bankrupt true.
3-day season ended 163 coins rep 98: 'Season over','Score: 261','Days: 3','Best: 261'; slot emptied; title had no Continue.
Records showed 'Score 261, 3 days, Easy' and 'Score 0, 2 days, Easy, bankrupt'; the five-cap, ordering among several and display in a later run were not checked.
Day 1 evening 'Stamp: First coin', 'Stamp: Sold out'; not repeated on day 2; Stamps screen 'First coin: yes'... 'Rain trade: no'; stamps kept into later runs on the same folder.
First coin on a day with sales; Full stall on a day opened with 8 crates; Whole season at day 3 of 3 with coins >= 0.
Sold out earned when crated apples/bread/flowers sold out; the negative case (good without crate) was not isolated.
After Continue in a later run the day's draws differ from the unbroken game (wholesale and order differed, see d17), so the day cannot be the same.
Repeated runs with seed 1 from fresh folders printed the same states (day 1 taken 102 in three runs); seeds 2-4 gave other forecasts, prices and visitor lists.
Escape on Evening, Left on title, put/finish/rush/left on Morning changed nothing.
modules/work/data/rules.json holds goods, visitor_types, hourly_rates, weather, upgrades, stamps; README 'Changing data' says how.
f_stall.png: text grid Back/Front with crate letters A/B/L, cursor [A], Good: Apples, Price: 4, Crates: 8 of 8, matching state.
f_day.png: stall rows, Aisle '. . . . . R16' (x 5), Queue, Till 1: R15, 10:11, Speed: Rush, Coins, Taken, Served, Reputation.
Frames on the Evening (both the README's own command and mine) show only the placeholder '{work.view_a}' and the engine warns 'nothing keeps work.view_a'; the evening's texts are not drawn.
README has How to play, where things are kept (settings.json in --settings folder) and the two commands, which run as written (the frame command's evening frame is the d60 defect).

defects: The season seed is saved as a JSON float and loses precision, so a season continued in a later run redraws its saved day differently.
Quit does not end a headless run; the printed tick is the full --ticks count.
Evening frames render '{work.view_a}' instead of the screen.
could_not_check: d14: the 99-unit stock cap could not be reached affordably in a run.
d32: the price 5 cook and tourist 6/7 cases were not run within the judge budget.
d35: batch order of removal not observed (every unit sold).
d37: no walk-out ever occurred in the runs made.
d40: Sign effect not observable on the day it was owned.
d42: fish spoiling on the following non-heat evening not observed.
d50: multi-record ordering, five-cap and later-run display not run.
d53: the no-crate negative case not isolated.
